answer: Try a liveness video check with a random script. First, the agent's owner films their face while the screen flashes a fresh color sequence that has to bounce off real skin. Second, they read aloud an odd phrase drawn for that session only, like "karst caves under a wet meadow". Third, a model maps every facial vertex and compares the geometry against all enrolled hashes, rejecting near-matches. Faking 1,000 owners means hiring 1,000 real people at about $15 each, roughly $15,000, plus deepfake rigs that still fail the light test. A sybil farm here is a wax museum trying to blush on cue.
